column1: # Differences between kyo-email's reading of Content-Type and Content-Disposition values and Stalwart mail-parser's, over
# Kept by hand: HeaderCodecParametersTest prints, in this format, each row missing here and each row here that no longer occurs.
# The module's reading is HeaderCodec.contentType, or HeaderCodec.contentDisposition when that answers nothing. Each reading is
# written as type/subtype; name="value"..., or null.
# Columns, tab-separated: vector index from 0, header, the module's reading, Stalwart's reading, reason. Backslash, tab, CR and LF
# in a value are written as \\, \t, \r and \n, and any other control character as \uXXXX.
# Reasons, each the first rule of HeaderCodecStalwart.classifyContentType that holds:

#   InvalidContentType: Stalwart reads a value that is not a type, a subtype and parameters (no subtype, other text after the subtype, a character outside the token grammar) as far as it goes; the module answers no media type and no disposition, and the parser applies the default of RFC 2045 section 5.2

#   NameNotRfc2231: a parameter name holds a * outside RFC 2231's attribute [*section] [*] shape (*, 3**, 1 * 999); Stalwart reads such names by its own rules, and the module reads each as a plain parameter of that whole name, or skips it when white space splits it
#   LanguageAttribute: Stalwart reports the RFC 2231 language as a parameter named <name>-language; the module drops the language
#   WhiteSpaceBetweenAdjacentWords: Stalwart keeps the white space between adjacent encoded words in a quoted value; RFC 2047 section 6.2 ignores it, and the module drops it
#   FieldEndWhiteSpace: the value ends inside an unclosed quoted string; Stalwart keeps the white space at the end of the field, which the module's header reader removes

#   CharsetOnLaterSegment: a continuation segment after the first carries a charset'language' prefix; Stalwart removes it, and the module reads it as data, since RFC 2231 section 4.1 puts that information only at the beginning of the value
